problem: `explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:40-42` (87% of 39,287 samples are `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` under `TypeAnalyzer.parents`, 17,591, and `excludesClause`, 16,213; the capture's `:756`/`:786` are the shadow's lines for the tree's `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:726` and `:757`), measured on the stock tree here as the checker-count stage taking 22.3-22.6 s with the memo off (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/timing.txt:4-9`).
spec: `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:207-215` (a trait type is a subtype of every type in its `extends` clause and excludes every type in its `excludes` clause), with `:163-164` (subtypes of excluding types exclude each other) and `Specification/basic/traits.tex:187-192` (the extension relation is the smallest relation the declarations induce): the two memoized functions compute these relations from the declarations and the type's arguments alone; the prose says nothing about how a checker computes them (`grep -rn -i 'memo\|cache' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` finds no checker-implementation text).
precedent: `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch:656-716` (the prototype: one switch, `parents`/`excludesClause` routed through a memo, a global map keyed by `(traits, t)`), and the tree's memo shape `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:380-391` (`pExcMemo`: switch, `get`, compute, store), with one switch over two memos at `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53`.
deviation: the memo is a pair of per-table maps on `TraitTable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:81-97`), not a global map keyed by the table (`shadow.patch:710-716`), as the prototype's author asked (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:94-96`); the switch `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` is read on the table beside the maps, not in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`'s block (`:62-69`), so that `TypeAnalyzer.scala` changes at its two call sites only (`TraitTable.scala:82`); the two bodies are wrapped by a by-name argument (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722`, `:747`) instead of being split into a wrapper and an `Inner` function as the shadow and `pExc` do; the maps are `java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap` with `get`/`putIfAbsent`, not the `scala.collection.mutable.HashMap` of the tree's ten memos (`TraitTable.scala:83-84`, `:89-96`); no name visible to a Fortress program is added, so there is no specification spelling to differ from.
historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala`

## What landed

`TraitTable` gains a memo for each of `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `TypeAnalyzer.excludesClause`, both behind one switch, `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` (default on), 17 lines at `TraitTable.scala:81-97` plus two imports (`:15`, `:26`). In `TypeAnalyzer.scala` exactly two lines change, the two `def` lines: `parents` at `:722` and `excludesClause` at `:747` now pass their unchanged bodies to `traits.memoParents(t)` and `traits.memoExcludesClause(t)`. No line of `TypeAnalyzer.scala` is added or removed, so every line number in that file, including rung P's `:443-457` and `pExcInner`, is the same after this rung as at the batch base.

The count stage's table is identical line for line before and after (93 errors, 52 locations, the same `nat` crash, `#shadow` fresh), and so is the checker's full output behind it. The stage takes 9.5-12.4 s with the memo on against 22.3-22.6 s with it off (three alternating repetitions each, `probes/timing.txt`).

## What I inherited, and a setup step I took

Nothing: the worktree `/home/user/fortress-memo` and the branch `wip/rung-analyzer-memo` did not exist when this rung started (19:44 UTC; `git worktree list` showed the P, L and S worktrees only, and `git ls-remote` no such branch). After a 40-second poll for it I created both with the recipe in `explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md:103-109` — `git worktree add -b wip/rung-analyzer-memo /home/user/fortress-memo d610695c0c014001687e528fa9fd99078db6ea76`, `cp -a ProjectFortress/build` from the main tree, `mkdir tmp`, `git push -u origin wip/rung-analyzer-memo` — which writes the worktree's entry under the main tree's `.git/` and touches none of its files. The coordinator should know that the launch did not create this worktree.

One operational note: `ant compileAll` must run from the repository root; `ProjectFortress/build.xml` is a stub that fails with "Premature end of file" (`ProjectFortress/build.xml:14-19`, "THIS FILE IS DEPRECATED"). And `ant compileAll` deletes the tracked `default_repository/caches/global.map`; the worktree restores it with `git checkout` before every commit, and no commit of this rung carries it.

## Where this belongs

`parents` and `excludesClause` are `TypeAnalyzer` functions (`map/modules-and-phases.md:95`, the `types/` package; `map/spec-to-implementation.md:188`, the trait-type row, whose checker column is `types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`). For a component, `StaticChecker` makes one `TraitTable` and one `TypeAnalyzer` over it (`map/modules-and-phases.md:357`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java:213-214`), and every further analyzer of that check is made from the first by `extend` or `extendJ` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:768-772`), which pass the same table on and start every per-instance memo empty. The checker makes new analyzers constantly: `OverloadingChecker.scala:288`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:88` and `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:57,66` each replace their analyzer with an extended one per generic declaration, and `STypeChecker.scala:189,202` extend per generic scope. So a memo on the analyzer would be dropped at every generic declaration; the table is the object whose lifetime is the whole check of one compilation unit, and it is what the two functions read. That is where the memo belongs, and it is where the prototype's author said it belongs (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:94-96`).

The fix is not in a phase or in the library: the two functions answer the same question every time they are asked it, and nothing upstream can make them be asked it fewer times without changing the checker's algorithms, which is not this rung's charter.

## Precedent search

**The tree already memoizes ten things in the checker, and none of them on the trait table.** `TypeAnalyzer.scala` has seven, each a per-instance `scala.collection.mutable.HashMap` behind its own switch in the block at `:62-69`: `pSubMemo` (`:97`, used `:113-121`), `pExcMemo` (`:380`, `:384-391`) and the five normalize memos (`:504-508`, used `:523-611`). `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala` has two, `subtypeUAMemo` (`:90`) and `subtypeEDMemo` (`:148`), both behind the one switch `fortress.schema.subtype.cache` (`:53`, used `:95` and `:153`). `typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala` has one, `validOverloadingMemo` (`:441`, used `:453-458`), behind `fortress.analyzer.overload.cache` (`:77`). All ten have the same access shape — switch, `get`, compute on a miss, store, return — and I copied that shape.

**A precedent that had a defect, and the count.** The triage of 2026-09-22 found that `validOverloadingMemo` is keyed on a pair of declarations while its answer also depends on the other signatures and the oracle, and that it stores only `true`, so it hides 27-35 errors depending on build order (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:41`, "a memo in the overloading checker keyed on declaration pairs ... hides 27-35 errors"). That is the defect a memo can have: a key that omits an input. I checked the ten: nine are keyed on everything their function reads beyond their owner's fixed state (the analyzer's `env`, fixed per instance, for `pSub`, `pExc` and the normalize memos; the `TypeSchemaAnalyzer`'s analyzer, `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:52`, for the other two), and one, `validOverloadingMemo`, is not. So one of ten has the defect, and it is already on record; this rung does not touch it. The memo added here reads nothing but its table and its key (next section), so it cannot have that defect.

**The prototype.** `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch:656-716`: one switch (`probe.nat.noParentsMemo`, a system property), each function split into a wrapper and an `Inner`, the wrapper doing `getOrElseUpdate((traits, t), ...)` on a global `HashMap` in `object TypeAnalyzer`. Its author's own verdict: "a global `HashMap` in a companion object, keyed by the trait table, never evicted, not thread-safe; in the real edit it belongs on `TraitTable`, with the `ProjectProperties.getBoolean` switch the tree's other caches use" (`followup.md:94-96`). This rung does what that sentence says; the deviations are in the provenance block and argued under "The decisions".

## Why the memo changes no answer

**What the two functions read.** `parents(t)` reads `typeCons(n)` for the trait's name, that index's `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, and `t`'s arguments, and returns their substitution (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`). `excludesClause(t)` reads the same index's `excludesTypes`, `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, substitutes, and recurses on each substituted supertrait (`:747-762`). `typeCons` is the table's `typeCons` (`:714-716`, `TraitTable.scala:32-68`), and `substitute` is a pure function of its three arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzerUtil.scala:35-60`: a map from parameter names to arguments and a tree walk). Neither function reads `env`, the analyzer's only other state, nor any memo of the analyzer. So both are functions of the table and the type.

**The table does not change.** `TraitTable` has no mutator: its two constructor parameters, `current` and `globalEnv`, are never reassigned (`TraitTable.scala:31`), and the memo is created with the table and dies with it. What the table reads beneath it does not change during the table's life either: a `CompilationUnitIndex` wraps its type constructors in `CollectUtil.immutable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/CompilationUnitIndex.java:41`); the only mutators of a trait's clauses, `ProperTraitIndex.addExcludesType` and `addComprisesType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/ProperTraitIndex.java:43-49`), are called from `IndexBuilder.checkTraitClauses` (`scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:235,245,261`), which runs while the index is being built (`:175`), and from the unit-test helper `TypeParser` (`scala_src/useful/TypeParser.scala:131-132`), which does so before it makes its table (`:173`); `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters` have no setter (`TraitIndex.java:60,77`). Every place the checker, the desugarer or code generation "changes the trait table" in fact constructs a new one, with empty memos: the eight construction sites are `StaticChecker.java:213`, `Desugarer.java:121`, `CodeGenerationPhase.java:81,179`, `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:73`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingChecker.scala:52`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:58` and `TypeParser.scala:173`, and there is no subclass of `TraitTable`. A table can outlive a rebuilt index — `StaticChecker` rebuilds the component index after type checking (`StaticChecker.java:244`) and keeps using the analyzer over the old table for the second well-formedness check (`:263`) — but that is the tree's behaviour with or without the memo: the table reads the index it was built over either way, and the memo returns what that table would compute.

**What a hit can return that a recomputation would not.** Keys are compared by `equals`, and the AST's `equals` ignores source spans: `SpanInfo.equals` is true for any two (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/SpanInfo.java:46-55`), and `TypeInfo.equals` compares only static parameters and where clause (`nodes/TypeInfo.java:58-73`). So a hit for a type equal to an earlier key returns the earlier call's result, whose substituted arguments carry the earlier call's spans. Nothing else can differ: `TraitType.equals` covers the name, the arguments and the trait's static parameters (`nodes/TraitType.java:74-95`), which is all `typeCons` and `substitute` read. The tree's normalize memos already have this property (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:537-545` stores a normalized trait type under its name and arguments). I looked for it where it could show — located error messages and the serialized checked ASTs, which carry spans — and it does not show: see the differentials below.

**Recursion.** `excludesClause` calls itself from inside its own computation, so the memo cannot use `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`, whose mapping function must not modify the map (it throws `IllegalStateException: Recursive update` on a recursive insertion into the same bin); `memo` does `get`, computes outside the map, then `putIfAbsent` (`TraitTable.scala:89-96`), the same order as the tree's ten memos. A cyclic hierarchy recursed without end before the memo and still does; the memo stores nothing until a computation returns, and an exception (`typeCons`'s "Not in the trait table", a `ClassCastException` on a non-trait index) stores nothing either.

**Threads, the column the batch record names.** The checker runs on one thread: the JFR recording's 39,287 samples were "all on thread \"main\"" (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:8`), and there is no thread, executor or fork-join use in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/`, `scala_src/` or `repository/` (the one `ForkJoin` hit, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:651`, is a descriptor emitted into generated code). The four-thread gate runs execute compiled programs, and no file under `runtimeSystem/` names `TraitTable` or `TypeAnalyzer` (the 36 files that do are all compiler-side). So no two threads can reach one table in today's tree. The maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s all the same: values are immutable Scala sets computed from immutable inputs, so two threads that race on one key compute equal values, one `putIfAbsent` wins, and `memo` returns the stored one (`TraitTable.scala:93-94`).

## The test, and what it recorded

The rung declares `testIsStage`: there is no `.fss` program that can go red for a cache. The stage is `explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh`.

**Recorded before the edit** (after `ant compileAll` on the batch base, nothing edited): `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/checker-count-preedit.txt`, committed in `3264d93e6` before the edit commit. Key line: `#total	93`. It is byte-identical to the gate's comparand `explorations/compile-ladder/gate-baseline/checker-count.txt` (`diff` empty).

**Recorded after the edit** (after `ant compileAll` with the edit, switch at its default): `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/checker-count-postedit.txt`. Key line: `#total	93`.

**The diff of the two tables is empty**: every api row (`AnyType 0`, `FlatString 4`, `FortressBuiltin 18`, `FortressLibrary 110`, `List 2`, `NatReflect 0`, `NativeArray 0`, `RangeInternals 104`, `Stream 0`, `String 12`, `TypeProxy 0`, `Writer 0`), `#total 93`, `#locations 52`, the `#crash` line (`Not yet implemented at STypesUtil.scala:557`) and `#shadow` fresh. Nothing moved, api by api, and nothing was meant to. The checker's full output behind the table — 96 located error lines with their column ranges and messages — was also compared with the stock run's, and is byte-identical (the run's first `###` header line and last `### rc` line excluded, both constant).

**Manifest values.** `expectedCheckerCount`: none; the total does not change (93 on this branch), so the rung declares nothing, as the batch record's table already has it (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:64`, M's row, `—`). `expectedCheckerCrash`: none; the crash line does not move. `writesState: true` stays as the record has it.

## The differentials

All captured in `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/differential.txt`, with the scripts beside it (`libbuild.sh`, `ctdiff.sh`, `ct-names.py`). "On" is the switch at its default; "off" is `FORTRESS_ANALYZER_CLAUSES_CACHE=false`, which `ProjectProperties.getBoolean` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/repository/ProjectProperties.java:237-248`) reads through its environment fallback (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/useful/StringMap.java:109-125`, dots to underscores, upper case). The off side used its own cache directory, so each side compiled everything from source.

1. **The checker over the interpreter's library**, three times each way (`probes/timing.txt`): six tables identical to the pre-edit table, six full outputs identical to the stock run's.
2. **The compiler prelude**, rebuilt in library order each way: the five bytecode jars, 556 class files, byte-identical; the 14 analyzed-cache files (the checked, serialized ASTs, spans included) byte-identical.
3. **The compiler test corpus**: every unit a `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/*.test` file names, compiled once each way, stdout, stderr and exit code captured, then `diff -r`. The results are in `differential.txt` section 3, which the report's final numbers are read from.
4. **The analyzer's unit tests** — `OverloadingJUTest`, `ConstraintJUTest`, `FormulaJUTest`, `TypeAnalyzerJUTest`, `TypeSchemaAnalyzerJUTest`, `STypesUtilJUTest`, 19 tests — pass each way.

Not run, by the batch's rule: `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem`. The suite counts are the gate's.

## The timing, which is this rung's home-3 record

`probes/timing.txt`, made by `probes/timing.sh`: the stage end to end (javac of its two driver files plus the checker run), alternating off and on, three repetitions, on a four-core box shared with one other rung's agent (load1 1.9-3.5 at the starts):

| | rep 1 | rep 2 | rep 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| memo off | 22.3 s | 22.6 s | 22.4 s |
| memo on | 12.4 s | 9.6 s | 9.5 s |

The same stage on the stock build, before the edit: 23.9 s (real 23.921 s, user 33.705 s); on the memo build, the run that produced the post-edit table: 10.3 s. The compiler prelude's own build, one sample each way (`differential.txt` section 1): `AnyType` 29.5 s → 17.2 s, `CompilerBuiltin` 126.3 s → 77.2 s, `CompilerLibrary` 35.6 s → 30.5 s, the last two files about 2 s either way; 196 s → 129 s for the five. These are single samples under a shared load and are recorded as such.

**A correction to the batch record's framing.** The record says "the whole-library check 21 s → 13 s in the tree's own terms" (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:144`). The 13 s was measured on the `nat` shadow with the memo, against 32 s for the shadow without it and 21 s for the stock tree (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:62-67`); the stock tree with the memo alone had not been measured. Measured here, on the stock tree: 22.3-22.6 s → 9.5-12.4 s for the stage, of which a few seconds are the stage's javac of its driver.

## Measured defects and their homes

**The defect this rung repairs: the checker re-instantiates a trait's extends and excludes clauses on every call**, with `excludesClause` recursing over every supertrait, and this is most of the checker's time on the library. Repaired here. Its home is the committed timing capture `probes/timing.txt` and a ledger row that cites it (provisional row 354 in `record.md`), because the batch record assigns it there (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:146`, "the rung's home-3 obligation and its permanent record") and because no gated assertion can hold a timing: the gate measures counts and outputs, and a wall-clock threshold on a shared four-core box would be red on load, not on the defect. The rung's gated assertion is the one it can have — that nothing changes: the count stage's table, identical line for line.

**No other defect was measured.** The span property of a memo hit (above) is a property, not a defect: no answer depends on it, and the differentials looked for it where it could appear and found nothing. The `validOverloadingMemo` defect is the triage's measurement (`FACTS.md:41`), already on record, and not this rung's.

## Why the memo changes no answer

**What the two functions read.** `parents(t)` reads `typeCons(n)` for the trait's name, that index's `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, and `t`'s arguments, and returns their substitution (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`). `excludesClause(t)` reads the same index's `excludesTypes`, `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, substitutes, and recurses on each substituted supertrait (`:747-762`). `typeCons` is the table's `typeCons` (`:714-716`, `TraitTable.scala:32-68`), and `substitute` is a pure function of its three arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzerUtil.scala:35-60`: a map from parameter names to arguments and a tree walk). Neither function reads `env`, the analyzer's only other state, nor any memo of the analyzer. So both are functions of the table and the type.

**The table does not change.** `TraitTable` has no mutator: its two constructor parameters, `current` and `globalEnv`, are never reassigned (`TraitTable.scala:31`), and the memo is created with the table and dies with it. What the table reads beneath it does not change during the table's life either: a `CompilationUnitIndex` wraps its type constructors in `CollectUtil.immutable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/CompilationUnitIndex.java:41`); the only mutators of a trait's clauses, `ProperTraitIndex.addExcludesType` and `addComprisesType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/ProperTraitIndex.java:43-49`), are called from `IndexBuilder.checkTraitClauses` (`scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:235,245,261`), which runs while the index is being built (`:175`), and from the unit-test helper `TypeParser` (`scala_src/useful/TypeParser.scala:131-132`), which does so before it makes its table (`:173`); `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters` have no setter (`TraitIndex.java:60,77`). Every place the checker, the desugarer or code generation "changes the trait table" in fact constructs a new one, with empty memos: the eight construction sites are `StaticChecker.java:213`, `Desugarer.java:121`, `CodeGenerationPhase.java:81,179`, `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:73`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingChecker.scala:52`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:58` and `TypeParser.scala:173`, and there is no subclass of `TraitTable`. A table can outlive a rebuilt index — `StaticChecker` rebuilds the component index after type checking (`StaticChecker.java:244`) and keeps using the analyzer over the old table for the second well-formedness check (`:263`) — but that is the tree's behaviour with or without the memo: the table reads the index it was built over either way, and the memo returns what that table would compute.

**What a hit can return that a recomputation would not.** Keys are compared by `equals`, and the AST's `equals` ignores source spans: `SpanInfo.equals` is true for any two (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/SpanInfo.java:46-55`), and `TypeInfo.equals` compares only static parameters and where clause (`nodes/TypeInfo.java:58-73`). So a hit for a type equal to an earlier key returns the earlier call's result, whose substituted arguments carry the earlier call's spans. Nothing else can differ: `TraitType.equals` covers the name, the arguments and the trait's static parameters (`nodes/TraitType.java:74-95`), which is all `typeCons` and `substitute` read. The tree's normalize memos already have this property (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:537-545` stores a normalized trait type under its name and arguments). I looked for it where it could show — located error messages and the serialized checked ASTs, which carry spans — and it does not show: see the differentials below.

**Recursion.** `excludesClause` calls itself from inside its own computation, so the memo cannot use `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`, whose mapping function must not modify the map (it throws `IllegalStateException: Recursive update` on a recursive insertion into the same bin); `memo` does `get`, computes outside the map, then `putIfAbsent` (`TraitTable.scala:89-96`), the same order as the tree's ten memos. A cyclic hierarchy recursed without end before the memo and still does; the memo stores nothing until a computation returns, and an exception (`typeCons`'s "Not in the trait table", a `ClassCastException` on a non-trait index) stores nothing either.

**Threads, the column the batch record names.** The checker runs on one thread: the JFR recording's 39,287 samples were "all on thread \"main\"" (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:8`), and there is no thread, executor or fork-join use in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/`, `scala_src/` or `repository/` (the one `ForkJoin` hit, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:651`, is a descriptor emitted into generated code). The four-thread gate runs execute compiled programs, and no file under `runtimeSystem/` names `TraitTable` or `TypeAnalyzer` (the 36 files that do are all compiler-side). So no two threads can reach one table in today's tree. The maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s all the same: values are immutable Scala sets computed from immutable inputs, so two threads that race on one key compute equal values, one `putIfAbsent` wins, and `memo` returns the stored one (`TraitTable.scala:93-94`).

The fix is not in a phase or in the library: the two functions answer the same question every time they are asked it, and nothing upstream can make them be asked less often without changing the checker's algorithms, which is not this rung's charter.

## Precedent search

That is the defect a memo can have: a key that omits an input. I checked the ten: nine are keyed on everything their function reads beyond their owner's fixed state (the analyzer's `env`, fixed per instance, for `pSub`, `pExc` and the normalize memos; the `TypeSchemaAnalyzer`'s analyzer, `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:52`, for the other two), and one, `validOverloadingMemo`, is not. This rung does what that sentence says; the deviations are in the provenance block and argued under "The decisions".

## Why the memo changes no answer

**What the two functions read.** `parents(t)` reads `typeCons(n)` for the trait's name, that index's `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, and `t`'s arguments, and returns their substitution (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`). `excludesClause(t)` reads the same index's `excludesTypes`, `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, substitutes, and recurses on each substituted supertrait (`:747-762`). `typeCons` is the table's `typeCons` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:714-716`, `TraitTable.scala:32-68`), and `substitute` is a pure function of its three arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzerUtil.scala:35-60`: a map from parameter names to arguments and a tree walk). Neither function reads `env`, the analyzer's only other state, nor any memo of the analyzer. So both are functions of the table and the type, which is the whole of the memo's key and owner.

**The table does not change.** `TraitTable` has no mutator: its two constructor parameters, `current` and `globalEnv`, are never reassigned (`TraitTable.scala:31`), and the memo is created with the table and dies with it. What the table reads beneath it does not change during the table's life either: a `CompilationUnitIndex` wraps its type constructors in `CollectUtil.immutable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/CompilationUnitIndex.java:41`); the only mutators of a trait's clauses, `ProperTraitIndex.addExcludesType` and `addComprisesType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/ProperTraitIndex.java:43-49`), are called from `IndexBuilder.checkTraitClauses` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:235,245,261`), which runs while the index is being built (`:175`), and from the unit-test helper `TypeParser` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/TypeParser.scala:131-132`), which does so before it makes its table (`:173`); `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters` have no setter (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/TraitIndex.java:60,77`). Every place the checker, the desugarer or code generation "changes the trait table" in fact constructs a new one, with empty memos: the eight construction sites are `StaticChecker.java:213`, `Desugarer.java:121`, `CodeGenerationPhase.java:81,179`, `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:73`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingChecker.scala:52`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:58` and `TypeParser.scala:173`, and `TraitTable` has no subclass. A table can outlive a rebuilt index — `StaticChecker` rebuilds the component index after type checking (`StaticChecker.java:244`) and keeps using the analyzer over the old table for the second well-formedness check (`:263`) — but that is the tree's behaviour with or without the memo: the table reads the index it was built over either way, and the memo returns what that table would compute.

**What a hit can return that a recomputation would not.** Keys are compared by `equals`, and the AST's `equals` ignores source spans: `SpanInfo.equals` is true for any two (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/SpanInfo.java:46-55`), and `TypeInfo.equals` compares only static parameters and where clause (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TypeInfo.java:58-73`). So a hit for a type equal to an earlier key returns the earlier call's result, whose substituted arguments carry the earlier call's spans. Nothing else can differ: `TraitType.equals` covers the name, the arguments and the trait's static parameters (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TraitType.java:74-95`), which is all `typeCons` and `substitute` read. The tree's normalize memos already have this property (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:537-545` stores a normalized trait type under its name and arguments). I looked for it where it could show — located error messages, and the serialized checked ASTs, which carry spans — and it does not show: see the differentials below.

**Recursion.** `excludesClause` calls itself from inside its own computation, so the memo cannot use `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`, whose mapping function must not modify the map (a recursive insertion throws `IllegalStateException: Recursive update`); `memo` does `get`, computes outside the map, then `putIfAbsent` (`TraitTable.scala:89-96`), the same order as the tree's ten memos. A cyclic hierarchy recursed without end before the memo and still does; the memo stores nothing until a computation returns, and an exception (`typeCons`'s "Not in the trait table", a `ClassCastException` on a non-trait index) stores nothing either.

**Threads, the column the batch record names.** The checker runs on one thread: the JFR recording's 39,287 samples were "all on thread \"main\"" (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:8`), and there is no thread, executor or fork-join use in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/`, `scala_src/` or `repository/` (the one `ForkJoin` hit, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:651`, is a descriptor emitted into generated code). The four-thread gate runs execute compiled programs, and no file under `runtimeSystem/` names `TraitTable` or `TypeAnalyzer` (the 36 files that do are all compiler-side). So no two threads can reach one table in today's tree. The maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s all the same: values are immutable Scala sets computed from immutable inputs, so two threads that race on one key compute equal values, one `putIfAbsent` wins, and `memo` returns the stored one (`TraitTable.scala:93-94`).

The rung declares `testIsStage`: there is no `.fss` program that can go red for a cache. The stage is `explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh`.

**Recorded after the edit** (after `ant compileAll` with the edit, switch at its default): `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/checker-count-postedit.txt`. Key line: `#total	93`.

All captured in `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/differential.txt`, with the scripts beside it (`libbuild.sh`, `ctdiff.sh`, `ct-names.py`). 3. **The compiler test corpus**: every unit a `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/*.test` file names, compiled once each way, stdout, stderr and exit code captured, then compared; the bytecode and analyzed caches the compiles left compared too. `probes/timing.txt`, made by `probes/timing.sh`: the stage end to end (javac of its two driver files plus the checker run), alternating off and on, three repetitions, on a four-core box shared with one other rung's agent (load1 1.9-3.5 at the starts):

| memo off | 22.3 s | 22.6 s | 22.4 s |
| memo on | 12.4 s | 9.6 s | 9.5 s |

The same stage on the stock build, before the edit: 23.9 s (real 23.921 s, user 33.705 s); on the memo build, the run that produced the post-edit table: 10.3 s. The compiler prelude's own build, one sample each way (`differential.txt` section 1): `AnyType` 29.5 s → 17.2 s, `CompilerBuiltin` 126.3 s → 77.2 s, `CompilerLibrary` 35.6 s → 30.5 s, the last two files about 2 s either way; 196 s → 129 s for the five. These are single samples under a shared load and are recorded as such.

**A correction to the batch record's framing.** The record says "the whole-library check 21 s → 13 s in the tree's own terms" (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:144`). The 13 s was measured on the `nat` shadow with the memo, against 32 s for the shadow without it and 21 s for the stock tree (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:62-67`); the stock tree with the memo alone had not been measured. ## Measured defects and their homes

**The defect this rung repairs: the checker re-instantiates a trait's `extends` and `excludes` clauses on every call**, with `excludesClause` recursing over every supertrait, and this is most of the checker's time on the library. Repaired here. Its home is the committed timing capture `probes/timing.txt` and a ledger row that cites it (provisional row 354 in `record.md`), because the batch record assigns it there (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:146`, "the rung's home-3 obligation and its permanent record") and because no gated assertion can hold a timing: the gate measures counts and outputs, and a wall-clock threshold on a shared four-core box would go red on load, not on the defect. The rung's gated assertion is the one it can have — that nothing changes: the count stage's table, identical line for line, which the gate's eighth step checks on every future batch.

**No other defect was measured.** The span property of a memo hit (above) is a property, not a defect: no answer depends on it, and the differentials looked for it where it could appear and found nothing. The `validOverloadingMemo` defect is the triage's measurement (`FACTS.md:41`), already on record, and not this rung's.

## The decisions

1. **The switch is read on `TraitTable`, not in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`'s block.** The alternative was a `private final val` in the block at `TypeAnalyzer.scala:62-69`, the exact position of the analyzer's seven. Chosen: the table, because the batch record says "Nothing else in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`" beyond the two call sites (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:144`), because two lines added at `:70` would shift every later line of the file rung P edits (`:443-457`), and because a switch beside the state it guards is read once per table instead of once per analyzer (every `extend`). The name keeps the block's pattern, `fortress.analyzer.<what>.cache`.

2. **One switch for both memos, `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache`.** The alternative was one switch per memo, as the analyzer's block has. Chosen: one, because the two memos are one change with one reason, as in the prototype (`shadow.patch:667-668`) and as `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53` guards its two sibling memos with one switch; the JFR capture already attributes the time between the two (`f3-jfr-top.txt:41-42`). The name says what is cached: each trait's instantiated `extends` and `excludes` clauses.

3. **`ConcurrentHashMap` with `get`/`putIfAbsent`, not `scala.collection.mutable.HashMap`.** The ten precedents use the unsynchronized map and the checker is single-threaded, so the precedent would be as safe today. Chosen: the concurrent map, because the table, unlike the analyzers the precedents live on, is the one object every analyzer of a check shares, because the batch record singles out shared state for the four-thread column, and because the cost is nil at this call rate. `computeIfAbsent` was rejected for the recursion reason above.

4. **Wrap the existing bodies rather than split each function into a wrapper and an `Inner`.** The shadow and `pExc`/`pSub` split; wrapping keeps each `TypeAnalyzer.scala` edit to the one `def` line and leaves both bodies as they were. The cost is that with the switch off every call still passes through `memo`'s one boolean test.

5. **One comment line in the source**, at `TraitTable.scala:81`, stating the invariant the memo depends on ("sound while both depend on nothing but this table and the type"). It is an instruction to whoever next edits `parents` or `excludesClause`, not provenance, which is here.

Not run, and the subset is empty: this rung adds no name a Fortress program can see, the batch record names no ladder file for it ("No rung declares a ladder move", `CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:67`), and no recorded first error in `explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/raw/` names any of the added names (`grep -rl` for `memoParents`, `memoExcludesClause`, `cacheClauses`, `parentsMemo`, `excludesClauseMemo`, `clauses.cache`: no hit). content.content:
A trait type is a subtype of every type
that appears in the \KWD{extends} clause of its definition.
In addition, every trait type is a subtype of \TYP{Any}.

A trait declaration may also include an \KWD{excludes} clause,
in which case the defined trait type
excludes every type that appears in that clause.
Every trait type also excludes every arrow type and every tuple type,
---
Also note that if two types exclude each other
then any subtypes of these types also exclude each other.
---
That is, trait \VAR{T} \emph{extends} trait \VAR{U}
if and only if \VAR{T} explicitly or implicitly
extends \VAR{U} or if there is some trait \VAR{S}
that \VAR{T} explicitly extends and that extends \VAR{U}.
The extension relation induced by a program is the smallest
relation satisfying these conditions.
---

<!-- Rung M of climb batch 3 (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.md, section M): a memo for
     TypeAnalyzer.parents and excludesClause, held on TraitTable behind a ProjectProperties switch.
     Written 2026-09-22 by the worker that made it. One line per paragraph. -->

# Rung M: the checker memo

problem: `explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:40-42` (87% of 39,287 samples are `TypeAnalyzerUtil.substitute` under `TypeAnalyzer.parents`, 17,591, and `excludesClause`, 16,213; the capture's `:756`/`:786` are the shadow's lines for the tree's `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:726` and `:757`), measured on the stock tree here as the checker-count stage taking 22.3-22.6 s with the memo off (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/timing.txt:4-9`).
spec: `Specification/basic/types-vals-vars.tex:207-215` (a trait type is a subtype of every type in its `extends` clause and excludes every type in its `excludes` clause), with `:163-164` (subtypes of excluding types exclude each other) and `Specification/basic/traits.tex:187-192` (the extension relation is the smallest relation the declarations induce): the two memoized functions compute these relations from the declarations and the type's arguments alone; the prose says nothing about how a checker computes them (`grep -rn -i -w 'memo\|memoize\|cache\|cached'` over `Specification/basic` and `basic-lib` finds only `basic/matrix-unpasting.tex:52-53`, on cache-oblivious matrix multiplication; `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-analyzer-memo/probes/spec-grep.txt`).
precedent: `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch:656-715` (the prototype: one switch, `parents`/`excludesClause` routed through a memo, a global map keyed by `(traits, t)`), and the tree's memo shape `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:380-391` (`pExcMemo`: switch, `get`, compute, store), with one switch over two memos at `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53`.
deviation: the memo is a pair of per-table maps on `TraitTable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala:81-97`), not a global map keyed by the table (`shadow.patch:710-715`), as the prototype's author asked (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:96-98`); the switch `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` is read on the table beside the maps, not in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`'s block (`:62-69`), so that `TypeAnalyzer.scala` changes at its two call sites only (`TraitTable.scala:82`); the two bodies are wrapped by a by-name argument (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722`, `:747`) instead of being split into a wrapper and an `Inner` function as the shadow and `pExc` do; the maps are `java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap` with `get`/`putIfAbsent`, not the `scala.collection.mutable.HashMap` of the tree's ten memos (`TraitTable.scala:83-84`, `:89-96`); no name visible to a Fortress program is added, so there is no specification spelling to differ from.
historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/TraitTable.scala`

## What landed

`TraitTable` gains a memo for each of `TypeAnalyzer.parents` and `TypeAnalyzer.excludesClause`, both behind one switch, `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache` (default on): 20 lines added to `TraitTable.scala`: two imports (`:15`, `:26`) and the memo at `:81-97` with a blank line after it. In `TypeAnalyzer.scala` exactly two lines change, the two `def` lines: `parents` at `:722` and `excludesClause` at `:747` now pass their unchanged bodies to `traits.memoParents(t)` and `traits.memoExcludesClause(t)`. No line of `TypeAnalyzer.scala` is added or removed, so every line number in that file, rung P's `:443-457` and `pExcInner` included, is the same after this rung as at the batch base.

The count stage's table is identical line for line before and after (93 errors, 52 locations, the same `nat` crash, `#shadow` fresh), and so is the checker's full output behind it. The stage takes 9.5-12.4 s with the memo on against 22.3-22.6 s with it off (three alternating repetitions each, `probes/timing.txt`).

## What I inherited, and a setup step I took

Nothing: the worktree `/home/user/fortress-memo` and the branch `wip/rung-analyzer-memo` did not exist when this rung started (19:44 UTC; `git worktree list` showed the P, L and S worktrees only, and `git ls-remote` had no such branch). After a 40-second poll for it I created both with the recipe in `explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md:103-109` — `git worktree add -b wip/rung-analyzer-memo /home/user/fortress-memo d610695c0c014001687e528fa9fd99078db6ea76`, `cp -a ProjectFortress/build` from the main tree, `mkdir tmp`, `git push -u origin wip/rung-analyzer-memo` — which writes the worktree's entry under the main tree's `.git/` and touches none of the main tree's files. The coordinator should know that the launch did not create this worktree.

Two operational notes. `ant compileAll` must run from the repository root; `ProjectFortress/build.xml` is a stub that fails with "Premature end of file" (`ProjectFortress/build.xml:14-18`, "THIS FILE IS DEPRECATED"). And `ant compileAll` deletes the tracked `default_repository/caches/global.map`; the worktree restores it with `git checkout` before committing, and no commit of this rung carries it.

## Where this belongs

`parents` and `excludesClause` are `TypeAnalyzer` functions (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:95`, the `types/` package; `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:188`, the trait-type row, whose checker column is `types/TypeAnalyzer.scala`). For a component, `StaticChecker` makes one `TraitTable` and one `TypeAnalyzer` over it (`map/modules-and-phases.md:357`; `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java:213-214`), and every further analyzer of that check is made from the first by `extend` or `extendJ` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:768-772`), which pass the same table on and start every per-instance memo empty. The checker makes new analyzers constantly: `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:288`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:88` and `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:57,66,76,85` each replace their analyzer with an extended one per generic declaration, and `STypeChecker.scala:189,202` extend per generic scope. So a memo on the analyzer would be dropped at every generic declaration; the table is the object whose lifetime is the whole check of one compilation unit, and it is what the two functions read. That is where the memo belongs, and where the prototype's author said it belongs (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup.md:96-98`).

The fix is not in a phase or in the library: the two functions answer the same question every time they are asked it, and nothing upstream can make them be asked less often without changing the checker's algorithms, which is not this rung's charter.

## Precedent search

**The tree already memoizes ten things in the checker, and none of them on the trait table.** `TypeAnalyzer.scala` has seven, each a per-instance `scala.collection.mutable.HashMap` behind its own switch in the block at `:62-69`: `pSubMemo` (`:97`, used `:113-121`), `pExcMemo` (`:380`, used `:384-391`) and the five normalize memos (`:504-508`, used `:523-611`). `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala` has two, `subtypeUAMemo` (`:90`) and `subtypeEDMemo` (`:148`), both behind the one switch `fortress.schema.subtype.cache` (`:53`, used `:95` and `:153`). `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala` has one, `validOverloadingMemo` (`:441`, used `:453-458`), behind `fortress.analyzer.overload.cache` (`:77`). All ten have one access shape — switch, `get`, compute on a miss, store, return — and I copied that shape.

**A precedent with a defect, and the count.** The triage of 2026-09-22 found that `validOverloadingMemo` is keyed on a pair of declarations while its answer also depends on the other signatures and the oracle, and that it stores only `true`, so it hides 27-35 errors depending on build order (`explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md:41`). That is the defect a memo can have: a key that omits an input. I checked the ten: nine are keyed on everything their function reads beyond their owner's fixed state (the analyzer's `env`, fixed per instance, for `pSub`, `pExc` and the normalize memos; the `TypeSchemaAnalyzer`'s analyzer, `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:52`, for the other two), and one, `validOverloadingMemo`, is not. So one of ten has the defect, it is already on record, and this rung does not touch it. The memo added here reads nothing but its table and its key (next section), so it cannot have that defect.

**The prototype.** `explorations/perf-probes/nat/shadow.patch:656-715`: one switch (`probe.nat.noParentsMemo`, a system property), each function split into a wrapper and an `Inner`, the wrapper doing `getOrElseUpdate((traits, t), ...)` on a global `HashMap` in `object TypeAnalyzer`. Its author's own verdict: "a global `HashMap` in a companion object, keyed by the trait table, never evicted, not thread-safe; in the real edit it belongs on `TraitTable`, with the `ProjectProperties.getBoolean` switch the tree's other caches use" (`followup.md:96-98`). This rung does what that sentence says; the deviations are in the provenance block and argued under "The decisions".

**What the two functions read.** `parents(t)` reads `typeCons(n)` for the trait's name, that index's `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, and `t`'s arguments, and returns their substitution (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:722-727`). `excludesClause(t)` reads the same index's `excludesTypes`, `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters`, substitutes, and recurses on each substituted supertrait (`:747-762`). `typeCons` is the table's `typeCons` (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-710`, `TraitTable.scala:33-74`), and `substitute` is a pure function of its three arguments (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzerUtil.scala:35-60`: a map from parameter names to arguments and a tree walk). Neither function reads `env`, the analyzer's only other state, nor any memo of the analyzer. So both are functions of the table and the type, which is the whole of the memo's key and owner.

**The table does not change.** `TraitTable` has no mutator: its two constructor parameters, `current` and `globalEnv`, are never reassigned (`TraitTable.scala:32`), and the memo is created with the table and dies with it. What the table reads beneath it does not change during the table's life either: a `CompilationUnitIndex` wraps its type constructors in `CollectUtil.immutable` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/CompilationUnitIndex.java:41`); the only mutators of a trait's clauses, `ProperTraitIndex.addExcludesType` and `addComprisesType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/ProperTraitIndex.java:43-49`), are called from `IndexBuilder.checkTraitClauses` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/IndexBuilder.scala:235,245,261`), which runs while the index is being built (`:175`), and from the unit-test helper `TypeParser` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/TypeParser.scala:131-132`), which does so before it makes its table (`:173`); `extendsTypes` and `staticParameters` have no setter (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/index/TraitIndex.java:60,77`). Every place the checker, the desugarer or code generation "changes the trait table" in fact constructs a new one, with empty memos: the eight construction sites are `StaticChecker.java:213`, `Desugarer.java:121`, `CodeGenerationPhase.java:81,179`, `scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:73`, `scala_src/overloading/OverloadingChecker.scala:52`, `AbstractMethodChecker.scala:58` and `TypeParser.scala:173`, and `TraitTable` has no subclass. A table can outlive a rebuilt index — `StaticChecker` rebuilds the component index after type checking (`StaticChecker.java:248`) and keeps using the analyzer over the old table for the second well-formedness check (`:268`) — but that is the tree's behaviour with or without the memo: the table reads the index it was built over either way, and the memo returns what that table would compute.

**What a hit can return that a recomputation would not.** Keys are compared by `equals`, and the AST's `equals` ignores source spans: `SpanInfo.equals` is true for any two (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/SpanInfo.java:46-55`), and `TypeInfo.equals` compares only static parameters and where clause (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TypeInfo.java:58-73`). So a hit for a type equal to an earlier key returns the earlier call's result, whose substituted arguments carry the earlier call's spans. Nothing else can differ: `TraitType.equals` covers the name, the arguments and the trait's static parameters (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nodes/TraitType.java:74-95`), which is all `typeCons` and `substitute` read. The tree's normalize memos already have this property (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:537-545` stores a normalized trait type under its name and arguments). I looked for it where it could show — located error messages, and the serialized checked ASTs, which carry spans — and it does not show: see the differentials below.

**Recursion.** `excludesClause` calls itself from inside its own computation, so the memo cannot use `ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent`, whose mapping function must not modify the map (a recursive insertion throws `IllegalStateException: Recursive update`); `memo` does `get`, computes outside the map, then `putIfAbsent` (`TraitTable.scala:89-96`), the same order as the tree's ten memos. A cyclic hierarchy recursed without end before the memo and still does; the memo stores nothing until a computation returns, and an exception (`typeCons`'s "Not in the trait table", a `ClassCastException` on a non-trait index) stores nothing either.

**Threads, the column the batch record names.** The checker runs on one thread: the JFR recording's 39,287 samples were "all on thread \"main\"" (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/followup/f3-jfr-top.txt:8`), and there is no thread, executor or fork-join use in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/`, `scala_src/` or `repository/` (the one `ForkJoin` hit, `compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:651`, is a descriptor emitted into generated code). The four-thread gate runs execute compiled programs, and no file under `runtimeSystem/` names `TraitTable` or `TypeAnalyzer` (the 37 files that do are all compiler-side: under `compiler/`, `scala_src/` and `repository/ForeignJava.java`). So no two threads can reach one table in today's tree. The maps are `ConcurrentHashMap`s all the same: values are immutable Scala sets computed from immutable inputs, so two threads that race on one key compute equal values, one `putIfAbsent` wins, and `memo` returns the stored one (`TraitTable.scala:93-94`).

## The test, and what it recorded

Chosen: the table, because the batch record says "Nothing else in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`" beyond the two call sites (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:146`), because two lines added at `:70` would shift every later line of the file rung P edits (`:443-457`), and because a switch beside the state it guards is read once per table instead of once per analyzer (every `extend`). The name keeps the block's pattern, `fortress.analyzer.<what>.cache`.

2. **One switch for both memos, `fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache`.** The alternative was one switch per memo, as the analyzer's block has. Chosen: one, because the two memos are one change with one reason, as in the prototype (`shadow.patch:667-668`) and as `TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53` guards its two sibling memos with one switch; the JFR capture already attributes the time between the two (`f3-jfr-top.txt:41-42`). toolu_01QA7KhGzGpHdPML9AgfFZjM.summary:
The rung landed. TypeAnalyzer.parents and excludesClause are now memoized on TraitTable behind one switch, fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache (default on). In TypeAnalyzer.scala only the two def lines (:722, :747) change: each passes its unchanged body to traits.memoParents or traits.memoExcludesClause. No line is added there, so rung P's line numbers are unchanged. TraitTable gains 20 lines: ConcurrentHashMap maps filled by get then putIfAbsent, because excludesClause recurses into its own map.
Soundness: both functions read only the table and the type (typeCons, and the pure substitute). TraitTable has no mutator. The index clauses change only while an index is being built. Every "new" trait table is a new object with empty memos (eight construction sites). The checker is single-threaded.
The count-stage table is identical line for line: 93 before and after. Differentials, memo on against off: the prelude's 556 class files and 14 analyzed-cache files are byte-identical. All 435 compiler_tests units give identical compile output, and the 2,049 class files and 230 analyzed-cache files they leave are identical. Six analyzer JUnit classes pass both ways.
Timing (probes/timing.txt): the stage takes 22.3-22.6 s with the memo off and 9.5-12.4 s with it on. The prelude build took 196 s off and 129 s on (one run each).
The batch record's "21 s to 13 s" compared the nat shadow with the stock tree. Setup: the launch had not created this worktree or branch, so the rung created both from d610695c0 with the recipe in remote-container.md. Suites not run, by the batch rule.
decisions: The switch is read on TraitTable beside the memo, not in TypeAnalyzer.scala's block of seven at :62-69. Rejected alternative: a val in that block (the exact precedent position). Reasons: the brief says nothing else in TypeAnalyzer.scala should change, and two lines added there would shift every line of the file rung P edits.

One switch for both memos (fortress.analyzer.clauses.cache). Rejected alternative: one switch per memo, as the analyzer's block does. The single switch follows the prototype (shadow.patch:667-668) and TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala:53, which guards its two sibling memos with one switch.

The maps are java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap, filled by get then putIfAbsent. Rejected alternative: scala.collection.mutable.HashMap, which all ten existing checker memos use. The table is the object every analyzer of a check shares, the concurrent map costs nothing, and computeIfAbsent was rejected because excludesClause recurses into the same map.

Each existing body is wrapped in a by-name argument at its def line. Rejected alternative: splitting each function into a wrapper plus an Inner function, as the shadow and pExc/pSub do. Wrapping keeps both bodies byte-identical and each TypeAnalyzer edit to one line.

One comment line in the source (TraitTable.scala:81) states the invariant the memo relies on. Rejected alternative: no comment. The line tells the next editor of parents or excludesClause what must stay true; it is not provenance.
defectHomes: Home 3, by the batch record's designation (CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:148): the checker re-instantiated a trait's extends and excludes clauses on every call, 87% of JFR samples. The defect is repaired in this rung, but no gated assertion can hold a timing. Its home is the committed capture probes/timing.txt (with timing.sh) plus provisional ledger row 354, drafted in record.md. The gated assertion that is possible (the count table is unchanged) is in place.

No other defect was measured. A memo hit returns substituted arguments that carry the earlier caller's spans, because AST equals ignores spans. The tree's normalize memos share this property, and no output, class file or serialized AST differed, so it is recorded as a property, not a defect. The validOverloadingMemo key defect was measured by the triage (FACTS.md:41) and is not this rung's.
divergences: None between walk and the compiled run: the rung changes only the compile path's static checker, and the interpreter never runs it.
